mission_08: You have implemented cross-validation strategies specifically designed for meta-learning, where the unit of analysis is the task rather than the individual data point. Leave-one-task-out provides the most conservative estimate of generalization to new tasks. Stratified k-fold ensures representative task distributions across folds, which is important when tasks vary in difficulty or domain. Nested cross-validation is essential for honest hyperparameter evaluation — without it, you risk selecting hyperparameters that overfit to your validation tasks. Task augmentation increases the effective sample size for more stable estimates. These CV strategies are critical for reliable meta-learning research and practice, as they prevent the common pitfall of reporting performance on tasks that are too similar to the training distribution.
